title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code Jul 18 changelog — /fork runs as a background session, plus a session-wide WebSearch cap and new subagent/Bash safeguards
bullets.summary: The Jul 18 Claude Code release lets /fork copy the conversation into its own background session so the main session keeps working, adds a session-wide WebSearch limit (default 200, tunable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION), hardens safeguards around WebSearch/subagent spawns/Bash, and fixes the bug where returning to claude silently killed running subagents and re-ran the prompt from scratch — plus reliability fixes across MCP, worktrees, telemetry, and remote sessions.
bullets.how: The Construct runs fan-out subagent jobs where 'silently stopped and restarted from scratch' is exactly the failure that wastes a run; the fix plus the background-/fork model is directly useful to our fleet, and the WebSearch cap is a real governance lever for scans like this one. Set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION deliberately rather than inheriting the 200 default.

bullets.title: Gemini Omni Flash lands in Google Vids (Jul 17) — conversational video editing + personal avatars from a text prompt
bullets.summary: Google put Omni Flash inside Google Vids on Jul 17: edit existing video with plain-text prompts and generate new clips with an avatar that looks and sounds like you. The underlying model (developer API since Jun 30) takes any mix of text/image/audio/video in and outputs physics-aware video at $0.10 per second, with conversational editing as its differentiator versus every other API video model.
bullets.how: Squarely on Brand 9 Signs' surface (short-form video for signage clients, social cuts) and on Vector's remit in The Construct, but we already route generative video/image through the Higgsfield MCP fleet. Worth one bench: does conversational text-prompt editing at $0.10/sec beat our current pipeline on a real B9S social cut, or is it a second vendor we don't need? Test, don't adopt on a launch post.

bullets.title: MCP specification 2026-07-28 goes final in 9 days — the largest breaking revision since launch (carried)
bullets.summary: The maintainers' RC stands: the core goes stateless (the initialize/initialized handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header are removed; any request can land on any instance), Streamable HTTP now requires Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name routing headers, list/read results carry ttlMs and cacheScope, authorization aligns to OAuth/OpenID Connect, and the missing-resource error moves from custom -32002 to standard -32602. SDK betas (Python v2 FastMCP->MCPServer; TypeScript v2 ESM-only, split into server/client packages; Go v1.7.0-pre.1; C# 2.0.0-preview.1) are out now.
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs is on the far side of a breaking change in 9 days. Two exposures remain live: any code matching the literal -32002, and any skill assuming session-scoped state the transport will no longer carry. The /doctor pass is the vehicle — produce the unused-server list and the Jul-28 migration inventory in one sitting, before the deadline, not on Jul 29.

bullets.title: arXiv 'Context Engineering: From Prompts to Corporate Multi-Agent Architecture' — five context-quality criteria for a governed fleet
bullets.summary: The paper reframes context management for enterprise agent fleets around five quality criteria — relevance, sufficiency, isolation, economy, provenance — and introduces 'intent engineering': encoding organizational goals, values, and trade-off hierarchies into the agent infrastructure itself rather than into individual prompts.
bullets.how: A clean vocabulary for what The Construct already does ad hoc across its skill/MCP fleet; 'economy' and 'provenance' map exactly onto the two things this scan keeps relearning (context cost of unused servers; never letting an unconfirmed detail age into fact). A framework to borrow for the installed-skills registry and memory system — read it against our CLAUDE.md governance and the /doctor output, not a tool to install.

praxis_lesson: Two of today's four items are things we should bench, not adopt — the Claude Code /fork background model and Gemini Omni Flash in Vids both look useful, but 'useful in a launch post' and 'useful on a real B9S/Construct job' are different claims, and only the second earns a slot in the fleet. The disciplined move this week is one instrument doing double duty: run a single /doctor pass that yields both the unused-MCP-server list and the Jul-28 migration inventory before the deadline, and use the arXiv five-criteria frame (economy, provenance) to decide what actually stays.
